verifications.claim: The Michigan "Fab Five" refers to the 1991 University of Michigan men's basketball recruiting class—Chris Webber, Jalen Rose, Juwan Howard, Jimmy King, and Ray Jackson.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Michigan’s “Fab Five” made up one of the best college basketball recruiting classes ever. ... Chris Webber, Jalen Rose, Juwan Howard, Jimmy King and Ray Jackson'; R3: 'The Fab Five was the 1991 University of Michigan men's basketball team recruiting class ... Chris Webber (#4) and Jalen Rose (#5), Chicago native Juwan Howard (#25), and two recruits from Texas: Plano's Jimmy King (#24) and Austin's Ray Jackson (#21)'
verifications.reasoning: Directly names the members and specifies 1991 recruiting class in both R1 and R3.

verifications.claim: The Fab Five were the first all-freshman starting lineup to reach the NCAA title game.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'the first all-freshman starting lineup to reach the national title game'; R3: 'The Fab Five were the first team in NCAA history to compete in the championship game with all-freshman starters'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly stated as first in both sources.

verifications.claim: The Fab Five reached consecutive national championship games in 1992 and 1993.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'took Michigan to consecutive national title games in 1992 and 1993'; R3: 'reached the 1992 and 1993 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship games'; R4: 'led the Wolverines to consecutive national championship game appearances in 1992 and 1993'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm consecutive appearances in 1992 and 1993.

verifications.claim: The Fab Five members are Chris Webber (#4), Jalen Rose (#5), Juwan Howard (#25), Jimmy King (#24), and Ray Jackson (#21).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Chris Webber (#4) and Jalen Rose (#5), Chicago native Juwan Howard (#25), and two recruits from Texas: Plano's Jimmy King (#24) and Austin's Ray Jackson (#21)'
verifications.reasoning: Exact match of names and jersey numbers.

verifications.claim: The Fab Five popularized baggy shorts.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'transcended the game with their swagger and progressive on-court fashion'; R3: 'wore ... baggy basketball shorts, which were an affront to conventional college basketball attire ... trend-setting but controversial antics'
verifications.reasoning: Sources attribute trend-setting fashion including baggy shorts to them.

verifications.claim: The Fab Five popularized black socks.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'wore black athletic shoes, black athletic socks, and baggy basketball shorts, which were an affront to conventional college basketball attire ... trend-setting'
verifications.reasoning: Directly mentions wearing black socks as part of their trend-setting attire.

verifications.claim: The Fab Five brought a "street" style of play and swagger to the college game.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'transcended the game with their swagger and progressive on-court fashion'; R3: 'trend-setting but controversial antics on the court'; R4: 'revolutionized college basketball ... culturally influential'
verifications.reasoning: Swagger and cultural influence on style/antics supported, but 'street' style of play described more broadly.

verifications.claim: The Fab Five played in the 1992 NCAA championship game, losing to Duke.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'lost to Duke in 1992'; R3: 'lost to Duke 71–51 in the 1992 title game'
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation of 1992 championship game loss to Duke.

verifications.claim: The Fab Five played in the 1993 NCAA championship game, losing to North Carolina.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'to North Carolina in 1993'; R3: '77–71 to North Carolina in 1993'
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation of 1993 championship game loss to North Carolina.

verifications.claim: A scandal involving improper payments resulted in the University of Michigan disassociating from certain Fab Five members.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NCAA prohibited Webber from associating with for 10 years'; R2: 'ordered the school to disassociate from the three living guilty players until 2012 (Webber's ban extended through 2013)'; R3: 'NCAA also banned Webber from associating with the program for 10 years'
verifications.reasoning: Scandal involved payments; disassociation explicitly from certain members like Webber.

verifications.claim: A scandal involving improper payments resulted in the University of Michigan removing their banners.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Banners commemorating the 1992 and 1993 Final Four runs ... would be removed from the rafters ... the four banners were removed'
verifications.reasoning: Directly states removal of banners due to scandal sanctions.

verifications.claim: The Fab Five members reunited for an alternative broadcast during the 2026 Final Four.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'they’re reuniting ... part of an alternative broadcast'; R3: 'featured commentators on an alternate TV broadcast of the Wolverines' 2026 Final Four'; R4: 'reunite for a special alternate presentation ... Final Four National Semifinal'
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm reunion for 2026 Final Four altcast.

verifications.claim: Four of the five Fab Five members (Webber, Rose, Howard, King) played in the NBA.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Juwan Howard ... Chris Webber ... Jalen Rose ... Jimmy King ... all wound up playing in the NBA'; R3: 'Four of the five members went on to play in the NBA. Only Jackson did not'
verifications.reasoning: Exactly lists the four specified members; Jackson did not.

verifications.claim: Juwan Howard won two NBA championships.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'won two NBA championship rings with the Miami Heat ... won the NBA championship ... in 2012 ... won his second NBA Championship ... 2013'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly states Howard won two championships with Heat in 2012 and 2013.
